A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original membership-inference experiments on CINIC-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, plus empirical embedding and density-ratio analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds tabular/text evaluations, RMIA comparisons, alternate-backbone experiments, and defense evaluations.

M1.justification: V2 adds two-layer MLP attack models for tabular/text data and an embedding-bag text input (Section 4.2), extending v1's image-regressor implementation. The Gaussian score modeling, top-two-logit score, and membership decision remain unchanged, making this a limited architecture/input adaptation.

E1.justification: V2 extends v1's image evaluations to Texas tabular classification and 20 Newsgroups text classification. Appendix F additionally reports CIFAR-10 defense experiments. Some other appendix panels inconsistently say CIFAR-10 where headings or captions say CINIC-10, but the substantial addition of text and tabular coverage is clear.

E2.justification: V2 adds RMIA to the existing CINIC-10/CIFAR-100 comparison and evaluates it on the new text/tabular tasks (Figures 2 and 4). This substantially expands comparison against contemporary shadow-model attacks. LiRA and LOSS correspond to v1's shadow-model and marginal baselines; those names do not represent additional comparators.

E3.justification: V2 introduces AUC evaluation, GPT-2/MLP target-model protocols, ResNet-18/ViT controls, and weight-decay/DP sweeps. Its RMIA protocol permits unseen-class background samples at query time. The original image training recipe remains. The new text dropout protocol is inconsistent: Section 4.2 specifies 2/20 classes, whereas Figures 4 and 8 show five-class groups.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F add multi-class dropout sensitivity on CINIC-10/CIFAR-100, robustness to alternate target architectures, and evaluations of regularization and differential privacy, including utility tradeoffs. The earlier score-function ablation and embedding/density-ratio analysis are retained; moving or enlarging their displays does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for attack performance. Gaussian variance estimation remains part of attack construction rather than uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: V2 adds RMIA, text/tabular, AUC, backbone, and defense results. Existing image values also change: CIFAR-100 class-0 quantile-regression TPR at 1% FPR changes from approximately 0.8% in v1 Figure 3 to 4.6% in v2 Figure 2. The revised CIFAR-100 bars average approximately 3.2%, despite retaining 3.8% in the prose. V1's 4.1% in-distribution quantile-regression result is omitted; ImageNet curves and density-fit MSEs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 5.1–5.2, Theorem 5.3, its density-ratio assumption and calibration conclusion, and its proof are unchanged. The proof moves from v1's main text to v2 Appendix G; revised explanatory prose introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The central unseen-class problem, shadow-model failure, quantile-regression alternative, and transferability contribution remain. V2 expands the introduction's explicit empirical contributions to tabular and text domains, claiming up to 2× and 6× shadow-model TPR respectively, while retaining the principal image-based claims.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1 Section 7's substantive qualifications about access to sensitive query examples, obstacles for nonspecialist auditors, and unknown training data in black-box auditing. It also drops the discussion of shadow models' in-distribution advantage. Conversely, it adds an explanation for RMIA's failure, qualifications about AUC, and interpretations of defense effectiveness and accuracy costs.

D1.justification: V2 adds localized implementation details for tokenization, GPT-2 fine-tuning, MLP widths, and defense parameters, plus an LLM coding-use disclosure. Appendix A's image hardware, memory requirements, training times, and code provenance remain unchanged. No new code or data release is documented.

R1.justification: V2 adds RMIA, recent language-model MIA, and privacy-defense references, removes the GLIRA citation and discussion, and corrects shadow-model attribution from Carlini to Shokri. These targeted updates retain the basic positioning around unseen-class auditing, existing quantile-regression attacks, and universal adaptability.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contribution list, and attack motivation. It reorganizes the experimental narrative into image, text/tabular, and defense subsections, removes the discussion/limitations section, moves the proof to an appendix, and expands the appendix structure. These changes go beyond inserting additional experiments.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the main comparison with RMIA and revised legends/axes, adds several multi-panel figures and two defense tables, rearranges Figure 5 into one row, and relocates the score-function plot. Appendix H enlarges existing ImageNet plots rather than adding results. New display inconsistencies include Figure 10's AUC panels retaining TPR axis labels.

improvement.justification: RMIA comparisons and new domain, backbone, and defense experiments substantially strengthen the breadth of validation beyond v1. However, v2 removes practical limitations central to its auditing motivation and introduces conflicts affecting interpretation and reproducibility: two versus five dropped text classes, and a retained 3.8% CIFAR-100 average despite revised bars averaging about 3.2%. These substantive gains and unresolved reporting problems prevent a reliable overall quality judgment from the PDFs alone.
